items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The lowest people in the mortal world are the context of restriction
items.inference: This teaching should be kept secret with effort from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: Under what conditions may this teaching be given to a previously accomplished person?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person who has been tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
The section is numbered fifth
The section is called a chapter
items.inference: This marks the end of the fifth chapter in the text emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of the Kaula teaching become known?
premises: The speaker claims knowledge has arisen
The knowledge concerns the determination of Kaula
The cause is the grace of the lord of Kaulas
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in the teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The verse asks for clarification of both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and can this all be explained fully?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is unknown
The speaker requests a complete explanation
items.inference: The verse asks where the soul dissolves and requests that all these matters be explained.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that soul?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme
The soul is partless and eternal
The soul is free from illness and stain
items.inference: The soul is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, and free from affliction and impurity.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from illness, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is identified as the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul who is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated in living beings?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
This air is present in all beings
It is described as situated within them
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the physical body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body
At that moment a new designation applies
The designation is supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as he leaves the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching said to be heard and transmitted to the goddess?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
The goddess is addressed directly
The teaching has come down through tradition
items.inference: The teaching is heard in the ear as something received through an unbroken tradition.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What effect is attributed to merely hearing this knowledge, O fair-faced one?
premises: The means is this knowledge alone
The knowledge is received by hearing
The addressee is addressed as fair-faced one
items.inference: Merely hearing this knowledge is presented as having significant effect.
uncertainties: The main verb or result is carried over from the surrounding context.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by merely hearing this knowledge...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner is described as one who undertakes it
The result is associated with freedom from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a condition free from bondage.
uncertainties: The precise sense of kāṣāyaṃ in this context is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: But whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state free from bondage.

items.question: What benefits follow for one who becomes freed from all diseases through this practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
Association with yogis is mentioned
Union with them is attained
items.inference: Freedom from all diseases leads to union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching about the practice concerning the soul has now been communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: A teaching has been told
The content is the practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the addressed recipient
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved and fully endowed person may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one who is fully endowed and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: The exact sense of sarva+bhāva+upapannasya is interpretive.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose mind is firmly resolved.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
Its origin is from the yoginīs
Giving it is explicitly prohibited
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is removed?
premises: The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
A present change is asserted today
The body is now described as pure
items.inference: The body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is now declared pure.
uncertainties: The form deham appears accusative but functions as subject in context.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The wish is to hear a teaching
The teaching concerns the auspicious overcoming of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed by this teaching?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
Doubt is explicitly denied
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: The teaching is asserted without doubt to explain how death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I will tell you—there is no doubt—how death is destroyed.

items.question: What condition affects even the wise one at the tip of nectar and essence?
premises: The location is the tip of nectar
The means involves the tip of essence
Even a wise person experiences burning
items.inference: Even the wise one experiences a burning sensation at the tip of nectar and essence.
uncertainties: The physiological referents of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa are symbolic.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one feels a burning at the tip of nectar, at the tip of essence.

items.question: How should the breath be drawn in at the root of the tongue and palate?
premises: The practice is located at the root of tongue and palate
The breath is to be taken in
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: One should place awareness at the root of the tongue and palate and slowly drink in the breath.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows when this breath practice is performed for one full year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The condition is sustained practice
Old age and death are affected
items.inference: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to poison is claimed for the practitioner even when bitten by great serpents?
premises: The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
Poison is said not to enter
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the practitioner's body.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
